summary.text: Doug Jones is a lawyer and former U.S. senator, who served from 2018 to 2021 after winning a 2017 special election, and U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of Alabama from 1997 to 2001. He is running on expanding Medicaid, eliminating the state grocery tax and taxes on tips and overtime, raising the minimum wage, a one-year moratorium on data centers, and a citizen ballot-initiative process.

paragraphs.text: Born in Fairfield, Alabama; graduated from the University of Alabama (1976) and Cumberland School of Law at Samford University (1979).

Staff counsel to the Senate Judiciary Committee, Assistant U.S. Attorney (1980–1984), private practice, then U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of Alabama (1997–2001), where he prosecuted two Ku Klux Klan members for the 1963 Birmingham church bombing and indicted Eric Rudolph.
Won a 2017 special election for the U.S. Senate seat vacated by Jeff Sessions and lost re-election to Tommy Tuberville in 2020.
